title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident is an example of training-data poisoning as a deliberate influence operation. A large volume of content, over half a million words across 124 reports, was produced in nine days by an entity with no verifiable legal status, physical address, or named staff, and published under the appearance of neutral American policy research. The stated goal was not to attract readers directly but to insert that content into the data repositories that commercial AI models draw on, so that the framing would later be reproduced by chatbots without attribution to its source.

The failure this exposes sits upstream of model deployment, in the data-collection and curation stage. AI systems that ingest web content at scale have no reliable mechanism for verifying the institutional legitimacy of a source, and once a narrative enters training data it becomes difficult to trace or correct when a model repeats it. The operation was designed to exploit exactly that gap, using the appearance of volume and scholarly format to pass filters that might otherwise flag low-credibility sources.

What is not established is whether any commercial AI model has in fact incorporated this content, or whether the framing it promoted has measurably altered how any deployed system responds to questions about the relevant topics. The reporting describes intent and method, not a confirmed outcome in model behavior.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

A fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded by the Israeli government, published over half a million words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The reports addressed contentious topics including Palestinian prisoner torture, Israeli war crimes, and Gaza starvation, framing Israel's position as neutral research. The New York production company Piro Inc filed the operation as a foreign agent, and the institute appears to have no legitimate legal status, physical address, or named staff. The effort is part of a broader, tens of millions of dollar campaign routed through European advertising company Havas Media to shape how AI systems present arguments about Israel.

The campaign reflects broader Israeli frustrations with declining American public support, with recent polling showing Americans favor Palestinians more than Israelis for the first time and majorities expressing unfavorable views of Israel. Israeli officials have called the spending on public diplomacy efforts a failure. Researchers note the real concern is not website traffic but getting content into training data repositories that feed commercial AI models, where misinformation becomes difficult to fact-check since sources go uncited when chatbots regurgitate trained narratives.
